subject: Physics

mods.t: Waves and the particle nature of light

cards: How close a measurement is to the **true value**
How close **repeated measurements** of the same quantity are **to each other**
Define the resolution of a measuring instrument.
The **smallest change** in the quantity being measured that produces a change in the reading
An error that makes every reading differ from the true value by the **same amount or in the same direction**
An **unpredictable** **scatter** of readings about the true value
A quantity that has both **magnitude and direction**
The distance moved **in a specified direction**
The **maximum velocity** of a falling object, reached when the **drag force equals its weight**
State Newton's first law of motion.
An object remains at rest or continues to move with **constant velocity** unless acted on by a **resultant force**
State Newton's second law of motion.
The **resultant force** acting on an object is directly proportional to the **rate of change of its momentum**, and acts in the **same direction**
State Newton's third law of motion.
If body A exerts a force on body B, then body B exerts a force on body A that is **equal in magnitude**, **opposite in direction** and of the **same type**
The **gravitational force** acting on an object
Define the moment of a force.
The force multiplied by the **perpendicular distance** from the pivot to the **line of action** of the force
For an object **in equilibrium**, the sum of the clockwise moments **about any point** equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point
A pair of **equal and opposite** forces whose **lines of action are not the same**
Define the centre of gravity of an object.
The point through which the **entire weight** of the object appears to act
The upthrust on an object in a fluid is equal to the **weight of the fluid** it **displaces**
The force multiplied by the **distance moved in the direction of the force**
State the principle of conservation of energy.
Energy **cannot be created or destroyed**, only transferred from one form to another
The **useful output** energy divided by the **total input** energy
The extension of a spring is **directly proportional** to the force applied, provided the **limit of proportionality** is not exceeded
Deformation in which the object **returns to its original shape** when the deforming **force is removed**
**Permanent** deformation: the object **does not return to its original shape** when the deforming force is removed
The tensile force **per unit cross-sectional area**
The tensile **stress** divided by the tensile **strain**, provided the **limit of proportionality** is not exceeded
Define the ultimate tensile strength of a material.
The **maximum stress** a material can withstand before it breaks
A material that breaks with **little or no plastic deformation**
The product of an object's **mass** and its **velocity**
State the principle of conservation of momentum.
The **total momentum** before an interaction equals the total momentum after it, provided **no external force** acts
The product of a force and the **time for which it acts**
A collision in which the total **kinetic energy is conserved**
The charge that passes a point when a current of **one ampere** flows for **one second**
The sum of the currents **entering** any junction equals the sum of the currents **leaving** it
The energy transferred **from electrical energy to other forms** **per unit charge**
The potential difference across a component when **one joule** of energy is transferred **per coulomb** of charge
The energy transferred **from other forms to electrical energy** **per unit charge**
The **potential difference** across a component **divided by the current** through it
For a metallic conductor at **constant temperature**, the current is **directly proportional** to the potential difference across it
The resistance multiplied by the **cross-sectional area**, divided by the **length**
Around any **closed loop** in a circuit, the **sum of the e.m.f.s** equals the sum of the potential differences
What is the terminal potential difference of a source?
The potential difference across the terminals of a source: the **e.m.f. minus** the lost volts across its **internal resistance**
A component whose **resistance decreases** as its **temperature increases**
What is the mean drift velocity of charge carriers?
The **average velocity** of the **charge carriers** along a conductor
An oscillation that travels through a medium or space, **transferring energy** **without transferring matter**
The **minimum distance** between two points on a wave that are oscillating **in phase**
The **maximum displacement** of a point on the wave from its **equilibrium position**
The number of **complete oscillations** **per unit time**
Define the period of a wave.
The time taken for **one complete oscillation**
A wave in which the oscillations are **perpendicular** to the **direction of energy transfer**
A wave in which the oscillations are **parallel** to the **direction of energy transfer**
A transverse wave whose oscillations are in **one plane only**
Define the refractive index of a material.
The **speed of light in a vacuum** divided by the **speed of light in the material**
The **angle of incidence** at which the angle of refraction is **90°**
State the conditions for total internal reflection.
The light travels towards a boundary with a medium of **lower refractive index**, and the angle of incidence is **greater than the critical angle**
When two or more waves meet at a point, the **resultant displacement** is the **sum of the individual displacements**
Sources that emit waves of the **same frequency** with a **constant phase difference**
The **spreading out** of a wave as it passes through a gap or around an obstacle
How is a stationary wave formed?
By the **superposition** of two progressive waves of the **same frequency** travelling in **opposite directions**
What is a node on a stationary wave?
A point where the **amplitude is always zero**
The energy transferred when **an electron** moves through a **potential difference of one volt**
Define the work function of a metal.
The **minimum energy** needed to release an electron from the **surface** of the metal
The **minimum frequency** of electromagnetic radiation that releases electrons from the surface of a metal
The **sum** of the **randomly distributed** **kinetic and potential energies** of the particles in a system
The energy required **per unit mass** to raise the temperature of a substance **by one kelvin**
The energy required **per unit mass** to **change the state** of a substance **without any change in temperature**
The **lowest possible temperature**, at which the particles of a substance have **minimum internal energy**
The state in which there is **no net transfer** of thermal energy between objects, because they are at the **same temperature**
The number of particles in **one mole** of a substance
The angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an **arc equal in length to the radius**
The large increase in amplitude when the **driving frequency equals the natural frequency** of the oscillating system
What is the natural frequency of a system?
The frequency at which it oscillates when displaced and left to **oscillate freely**
The gravitational **force per unit mass** at a point
Two point masses attract each other with a force that is directly proportional to the **product of their masses** and **inversely proportional to the square** of their separation
Define gravitational potential at a point.
The **work done per unit mass** to bring a small test mass **from infinity** to that point
An orbit **above the equator** with a period of **24 hours**, moving in the **same direction** as the Earth rotates
The **force per unit positive charge** at a point
The force between two point charges is directly proportional to the **product of the charges** and **inversely proportional to the square** of their separation
Define electric potential at a point.
The **work done per unit positive charge** to bring a small positive test charge **from infinity** to that point
The **charge stored per unit potential difference** across the capacitor
Define the time constant of a capacitor-resistor circuit.
The time taken for the charge on a discharging capacitor to fall to **1/e**, about 37%, of its **initial value**
The magnetic flux density that produces a force of **1 N** on a **1 m** length of wire carrying a current of **1 A** **perpendicular** to the field
The product of the **magnetic flux density** and the **area perpendicular to the field**
The product of the **number of turns** in a coil and the **magnetic flux** through it
The magnitude of the induced e.m.f. is **directly proportional** to the **rate of change of magnetic flux linkage**
The direction of the induced e.m.f. or current is such that it **opposes the change** that produced it
Nuclei of the same element with the **same number of protons** but **different numbers of neutrons**
The **average time** taken for **half of the undecayed nuclei** in a sample to decay
Define the activity of a source.
The number of nuclei that decay **per unit time**
The **probability** that an individual nucleus will decay **per unit time**
What does it mean that radioactive decay is random?
It is **impossible to predict** when a **particular nucleus** will decay
What does it mean that radioactive decay is spontaneous?
The decay is **not affected by external factors** such as temperature or pressure
The difference between the **total mass of the separate nucleons** and the **mass of the nucleus**
Define the binding energy of a nucleus.
The **minimum energy** needed to **separate** a nucleus into its individual protons and neutrons
The **splitting** of a **large nucleus** into two smaller nuclei, releasing energy
The **joining** of two **light nuclei** to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy
When a particle meets its **antiparticle** and their total mass is converted into energy in the form of **photons**
Define the luminosity of a star.
The **total power output** of a star
The **distance travelled by light** in a vacuum in **one year**
The **mean distance** from the Earth to the Sun
The distance at which a radius of **one astronomical unit** subtends an angle of **one arcsecond**
The wavelength at which a black body emits radiation of **maximum intensity** is **inversely proportional** to its **absolute temperature**
The total power radiated **per unit surface area** of a black body is directly proportional to the **fourth power** of its **absolute temperature**
An idealised object that **absorbs all** the electromagnetic radiation that falls on it, and is a perfect emitter
The **recession velocity** of a galaxy is **directly proportional** to its **distance** from us
The **density** of a medium multiplied by the **speed of sound** in it
